sre-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: sudden p99 latency jump observed on dedicated-pool eu-west-1 for model:redwood-7b-small. Auto-pager triggered. Queue depth rising >700 for 4m. Investigating.
jamie (oncall): taking pager. pulling graphs now — which customers hit? @leo @support (triage-bot)
support (triage-bot): incoming support signals: 9 enterprise sessions reporting slow responses/timeouts (EU). No production errors logged yet, increased client timeouts.
carlos (infra): autoscaler backlog growing. scale requests accumulating, warmup handshake durations spiking to ~18-25s. registry pull times elevated for eu-west images.
maria (runtime): streaming tail stalls increasing. p95 moved 400ms -> 900ms, p99 1.1s -> 3.5s. KV coldpath hits correlate with warm slots joining. dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/d/pool/eu-west-latency
jamie (oncall): paste of quick metrics snapshot:
``
pool: dedd-eu-west-1
queue_depth: 730 -> 880 (4m)
p95_latency: 420ms -> 920ms
p99_latency: 1.1s -> 3.5s
warmup_handshake: 2.4s -> 21s
autoscale_queue: 12 -> 36 requests
streaming_stall_rate: 1.1% -> 5.8%
```
maria (runtime): warmup flow currently blocks on kv-sync step; handshake-proxy showing elevated 5xxs under load. hypothesis: registry slow pulls + serialized prefix load = tail latency.
jamie (oncall): we need quick mitigations to protect enterprise customers. options: 1) emergency pre-warm N slots (manual scale) 2) flip fast-warmup feature-flag to skip prefix KV pulls during warmup 3) throttle scale requests to reduce thrash 4) reroute high-value customers to hosted fallback region 5) deprioritize low-priority queues. What can we action immediately? @carlos
carlos (infra): I can do 1 and 5 now. Kicking a manual prewarm of 25 slots and lower priority for `low` queue class. Executing: 
``
infractl pool scale --add 25 --pool dedd-eu-west-1 --prewarm=true
infractl queue set-priority --pool dedd-eu-west-1 --class low --priority=10
```
sre-bot: :white_check_mark: scale request accepted; provisioning started. Estimated bootstrap 35s per slot (trying fast-warmup if flagged).
maria (runtime): I'll enable runtime fast_warmup flag for warm path to avoid blocking on kv-sync (non-persistent). Pushing config change as canary=4 then roll. Also patch handshake-proxy timeout to reduce 5xx under flapping.
jamie (oncall): can we mirror registry pulls to a local EU mirror to speed image fetches?
carlos (infra): yes switching to eu mirror now; nodes pulling images will use mirror. Also enabling short-term rate-limit on autoscaler from 50->10 reqs/s to reduce thrash.

sre-bot: :information_source: alerts adjusted: p99 threshold reduced to 2s for incident noise.

maria (runtime): after enabling fast-warmup + prewarm + mirror: metrics moving positive. queue_depth 880 -> 300 within 2m; p99 dropped from 3.5s -> 1.4s; streaming stalls 5.8% -> 2.0%. Handshake-proxy 5xxs reduced.
leo (product): initial customer impact note: ~9 EU enterprise customers saw latency spikes/timeouts; no data corruption. Support drafting update.
jamie (oncall): plan for next 30m: keep mirror + fast-warmup active, monitor autoscaler backlog. If p99 remains >2s after pre-warm completes, escalate to cross-team call and start customer reroute to hosted fallback for impacted accounts.
carlos (infra): pre-warm done. 25 slots added. autoscaler backlog cleared. Manual autoscale throttle seems effective.
maria (runtime): rolling fast-warmup to full pool. Adding instrumentation: per-slot coldpath count + kv-sync timings. Opening follow-up issues for handshake-proxy threadpool and registry-mirror adoption.
jamie (oncall): aggregated numbers 8 minutes after mitigations:
``
queue_depth: 300 -> 65
p95: 480ms
p99: 1.2s
streaming_stalls: 2.0%
```
leo (product): support posted interim update. No urgent escalations.
jamie (oncall): handoff notes: I'll remain oncall for 10 more minutes; otherwise handing to maria for longer watch. Root cause hypotheses: registry CDN/mirror latency + serialized KV prefix load during warmup + handshake-proxy instability under churn. Follow-ups: autoscaler rate-limit policy, fast-warmup GA, handshake-proxy resiliency, pre-warm safeguards.
